candidates.exact_span: bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric Class A bacteria limit and two distinct timing triggers (use/disposal vs. bagged sale/giveaway). Different readings of when each trigger applies, or which trigger governs a given event, would change which limit is compared to reported measurements (A), whether monitoring was required for that period (B), and whether absent bacteria data reflects a documented no-monitoring condition or missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricts which Class A compliance pathways are enforceable under Texas permits. If a facility relied on Alternative 5 or 6, a different interpretation of authorization could change which numeric/process limits are treated as applicable (A) and which associated monitoring obligations count as required (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - The temperature of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be maintained at a specific value for a period of time. See 503.32(a)(3)(ii) for specific information. This alternative is not applicable to composting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers the actual temperature value and duration to an external cross-reference while imposing a composting exclusion. Whether composting is present, and whether the external values are incorporated, affects which numeric limits apply (A), whether temperature monitoring was required (B), and whether missing temperature data is conditional non-requirement or unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets enforceable process-condition thresholds (pH > 12 sustained for 72 hours) that may function as compliance criteria. Interpretation of measurement timing, averaging, and whether pH was maintained for the full period would change limit-exceedance determinations (A) and whether pH monitoring was obligated during that window (B).

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Couples a numeric temperature threshold to a concurrent pH condition. Different readings of the overlap period, duration counting, or which measurements satisfy 'above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer' would change compliance comparisons (A) and the scope of required temperature monitoring (B).

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a post-pH-treatment percent-solids numeric criterion tied to a defined 72-hour endpoint. Interpretation of when the endpoint occurs and how percent solids is measured would change applicable limit comparisons (A) and whether solids monitoring was required at that stage (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Combines a mandatory pre-treatment analysis obligation with a numeric limit that may apply before or after treatment. Whether 'prior to pathogen treatment' or 'either before or following' governs a given sample affects required monitoring (B), which numeric limit is used for comparison (A), and how to classify absent virus results (required missing evidence vs. conditional non-requirement) (C).

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for viable helminth ova prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for viable helminth ova is less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same structure as the enteric-virus Alternative 3 language: pre-treatment analysis duty plus a limit with ambiguous timing. Different interpretations of sampling timing and limit applicability would change monitoring-obligation findings (B), exceedance evaluations (A), and missing-evidence classification (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque- forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight bas is) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a numeric virus-density limit with multiple timing triggers (use/disposal vs. bagged sale/giveaway). Which trigger applies to a given sludge handling event affects the enforceable limit used for comparison (A) and when virus monitoring was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The density of viable helminth ova in the sewage sludge shall be less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides a helminth-ova numeric limit with the same dual timing triggers as Alternative 4 virus language. Interpretation of the operative trigger changes limit applicability and exceedance results (A) and the monitoring periods deemed required (B).

candidates.exact_span: b. Four alternatives are available to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge. Alternatives 2, 3, and 4 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the Class B compliance menu but disqualifies three alternatives for Texas permits. Whether a facility's chosen Class B pathway falls within authorized alternatives changes which numeric/process limits are treated as enforceable (A) and which related monitoring requirements are in scope (B).
